transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

My family keeps saying my beliefs about the festival and people watching me aren’t real, but I know they’re true and I can’t be convinced otherwise. They are the ones who insisted I come here today, but I know what is actually going on.

Besides these beliefs, have you been hearing voices or seeing things that others don’t, or have you felt your thoughts or speech becoming confused? If so, did this all start suddenly within the last few weeks, or has it been going on for much longer?

Yes, late at night I hear a man's voice whispering behind my left ear, telling me that my family and the doctors are plotting to stop my mission. My daughter also says I talk way too fast and get easily distracted lately, but all of this—the voice and these strong beliefs—only started about two months ago when I got so energized with the festival planning. I never hear these things or feel this way when I'm just feeling low; it only happens when I am revved up like this.
During this energized period, have you also needed much less sleep than usual and felt unusually euphoric or irritable most of the day? Did these changes last for at least a week?

Yes, I barely sleep because my mind is constantly racing, often waking up after just an hour or two. My mood swings from feeling on top of the world to snapping and yelling at my family over the tiniest things. This has been going on much longer than a week, really for about two months now.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidate was [F30.2], and based on this conversation it remains the same. The patient describes a sustained period of markedly increased energy lasting about two months, with very little need for sleep, racing thoughts, pressured speech, distractibility, euphoric and irritable mood, and psychotic symptoms (fixed false beliefs and an auditory hallucination). The psychotic symptoms occur specifically during the energized state and not outside it, which supports the same candidate rather than shifting toward a primary psychotic condition.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a sustained period of abnormally elevated/irritable and highly energized mood lasting about two months, with markedly decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, pressured/fast speech, distractibility, and psychotic symptoms (fixed persecutory/grandiose beliefs and an auditory hallucination) occurring specifically during the energized state. This is most consistent with a manic episode with psychotic symptoms.
